item.title: Sevilla claim late derby draw against high-flying Betis
item.description: Defender Kike Salas scored a late equaliser against Real Betis to earn Sevilla a derby draw (JORGE GUERRERO) Kike Salas struck late to save Sevilla a point in a 1-1 derby draw against Real Betis on Saturday. Manuel Pellegrini's Betis, fourth, had taken the lead through Antony's deflected effort early in the second half. However, hosts Sevilla, sixth, equalised in the 91st minute with Salas's low drive, which Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles somehow let squeeze past him. Betis trail leaders Barcelona by six points before the Catalan giants host Villarreal on Sunday. Later Saturday, Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, second, host Celta Vigo, aiming to pull level with Barca at the top of the table. Elsewhere, Valencia earned a 1-0 win at Rayo Vallecano to provisionally move out of the relegation zone. Alaves defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-1 to climb up to eighth. rbs/nf

item.title: Chelsea’s deep and ongoing issues revealed by Leeds drubbing
item.description: By the end, amid what Xabi Alonso described as a “fragile moment”, even his own cultured touch had deserted him. As his Chelsea team tried to offer something in the final minutes of an utterly nothing performance against a brilliant Leeds United , the ball was easily cleared for a throw. Alonso, famed for his technique as a player, miscontrolled it towards his underwhelming bench. He’s now seeing his reputation as a coach plummet, as Chelsea fall to eighth. This 4-1 evisceration was not just Leeds’ first win at the home of their old Seventies rivals since 1999 – to add to how Tottenham Hotspur also won here a few weeks ago – but a second defeat in a row, and a fifth in 11 this season. And yet the very nature of it was still worse than any numbers can tell. Outside an early Emmanuel Emegha goal on his first start, there was nothing to speak positively about, and just nothing about Chelsea. Leeds found it easy to get at them, and they were soon rampaging through them. They could have been 3-1 up by half-time, after Noah Okafor’s well-taken equaliser, but it never looked like it would take long to get there in the second half. And, sure, Chelsea might well dispute the absurd-looking handball decision that eventually gave Dominic Calvert-Lewin his goal to make it 2-1, but they couldn’t dispute that it was coming. Leeds were rampant, Okafor soon lashing in his second from yet another poorly-defended set-piece. There, Austin MacPhee’s influence becomes just one more aspect to question about the first team. The manner of Brenden Aaronson’s goal, as he was allowed to just surge through the team, summed the afternoon up. Chelsea didn’t look a team. Leeds, by contrast, knew exactly what they were about in every moment of the game. They had an identity. Chelsea are instead looking to individuals. Emmanuel Emegha scored Chelsea’s goal (Reuters) They lost all cohesion once Moises Caicedo again went off injured, having already lacked any bite without Joao Pedro . The striker was nevertheless involved in what might actually have been one of the match’s most telling moments. As Cole Palmer went off, Chelsea coach Willie Isa seemed to gesture the forward towards the fans. There were admittedly very few left, and many of those had loudly booed on the final whistle. Palmer didn’t go over, and then seemed to have a few words with Joao Pedro, too. They didn’t look all that amicable. “We were disappointed,” Alonso said afterwards. Either way, there is probably a bigger point there, that emphasises how all this is bigger than the manager. Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s penalty sent Leeds ahead (Reuters) Yes, a coach as accomplished as Alonso should be doing better than this. There has been constant talk that some of the players haven’t found him as tactically sophisticated as they expected, something which has arguably manifested in how they seem to have got worse the more time he’s had with them – in the same way they got worse the longer this game went on. item.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
item.description: Malick Thiaw put Newcastle in front against Arsenal (ANDY BUCHANAN) Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze's strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta's men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side's second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James' Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya's final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. kca/nf

item.title: Cardinals make bad Carson Beck news official for Week 11 vs. Chiefs
item.description: Cardinals make bad Carson Beck news official for Week 11 vs. Chiefs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals have shuffled through multiple quarterbacks this season, starting with Jacoby Brissett for a few weeks. Gardner Minshew then got a chance, but he recently got hurt. Carson Beck stepped in, making his NFL debut and first start in Week 10. While he and the Cardinals struggled in a loss to the Los Angeles Rams , it was still nice to see Beck make his first appearance in the NFL. But the following practice week didn't go well, as back spasms sidelined him. Unfortunately, as Cardinals reporter Darren Urban shared , the team made it official: Beck is out and won't face the Kansas City Chiefs . Cardinals officially rule out Carson Beck "The AZCardinals officially downgrade QB Carson Beck to OUT for Sunday's game because of back spasms," Urban reports. "Josh Johnson gets the start in K.C." While this Cardinals team isn't contending for anything this season, one of the more important things to take away from this year is how their young players perform. It might have a low chance of happening, but if Beck impresses this season, they might have an interesting question to ask themselves at the quarterback position this upcoming offseason. But with Beck now set to miss Week 11 due to back spasms, that evaluation is on hold. Josh Johnson, the ultimate journeyman quarterback, will get the start for Arizona against the Chiefs this weekend. Beck isn't the only one this Cardinals' offense will be missing. Brissett and Marvin Harrison Jr. were traded; Minshew, James Connor, Jeremiyah Love, Kendrick Bourne, Michael Wilson, and Jalen Brooks are all out due to injury. MORE : Blake Corum extends impressive touchdown streak as Rams continue remarkable turnaround Tyler Allgeier, Zonovan Knight, Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins, Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay, and Harrison Wallace III make up the skill players for the Cardinals in Week 11. So, while seeing Beck play is important, it would not be a surprise if he struggled with such a lackluster supporting cast, especially going up against a tough Chiefs defense, like the tough unit he faced in his NFL debut. After Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and no touchdowns with two picks against the Rams in Week 10, he's now going to miss his next chance to start with a back problem. The Cardinals have officially ruled out Beck for Week 11, turning to Johnson as their fourth staring quarterback they've turned to this season. item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns arrives prior to the game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Senior Day on the Forty Acres as quarterback Arch Manning plans to participate in what could be his final regular-season home game at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium as the No. 5 Texas Longhorns host the Arkansas Razorbacks. An SEC championship game and College Football Playoff berth are on the line for Steve Sarkisian’s team, which lost its margin for error with back-to-back losses to unranked opponents in October before surviving a home test against then-No. 7 Ole Miss and road challenges at then-No. 18 Missouri and then-No. 21 LSU. Now Texas is hoping for the type of comfortable victory that has eluded the team in SEC play. At 2-5 in the conference, Arkansas represents a prime opportunity for one, although the Hogs proved how dangerous they can be in taking advantage of an injury to Gamecock quarterback LaNorris Seller to beat then-No. 17 South Carolina 34-6 last week. Pregame injury report Listed as questionable on the first three SEC-mandated player availability reports, Texas junior edge Colin Simmons was ruled out on Saturday in the report released 90 minutes before kickoff. Senior cornerback Warren Roberson was upgraded from probable to available, while sixth-year offensive guard Laurence Seymore is a game-time decision.

(Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Getty Images The Los Angeles Lakers sit on top of the Western Conference at 14-3, with the third-best offense in the NBA — behind an MVP-level start to the season from Luka Doncic — and a solid defense. Walker Kessler has been exactly what the Lakers hoped for as a big in the paint, and their moves for role players that better fit around Doncic — Matisse Thybulle, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, Quentin Grimes — have largely worked out. Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka has seen it, too, and thinks this team has a deep playoff run in them. Which is why he said in an interview on the Lakers pregame show that the team would be "active" at the trade deadline (hat tip Real GM ). "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see. We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great, and we hope it continues." Active is a broad term. The Lakers will be active talking to teams, whether they make a deal will depend on the players available, and the price. The Lakers' most critical need is to improve at backup center behind Kessler. Kevon Looney has largely fallen out of the rotation, leaving the Lakers playing small ball with Sandro Mamukelashvili or Jarred Vanderbilt at the five, or leaning into two-way big Carson Cooper. There may be better options available. The Lakers don't have draft picks of note to trade, but they have players, and while they are hard-capped at the first apron, they are a little more than $8 million below that line and have room to work.

Penn State has cleaned up its first contact when receiving serve, allowing its setter to choose between multiple attacking options and putting its pin hitters in better positions to score. Thanksgiving football is on deck and, for 48 teams, the playoffs beyond. With at least a third of the tournament spots still open according to GametimeCT's unofficial calculations , there's plenty of drama in the final week. After a somewhat lackluster first half of the season, the second half paid off with plenty of electric games, led by Ludlowe's 34-31 win over New Canaan on Oct. 30, a game which had a wild momentum swing and jumbled the GametimeCT Top 10 Poll . The season has featured some great quarterback play, highlighted by seven senior veterans , at least six of whom will soon be in the playoff spotlight. And the list goes deeper than just those seven. For the holiday week ahead, there are 56 games involving 111 CIAC teams, with Stonington's long-running series with Westerly (R.I.) accounting for that odd number. Thanksgiving week holds plenty of drama outside of the playoff picture, with trophies, rivalry wins and bragging rights part of the scene. And the names are definitely cool. item.title: Ludlowe wins 1st CIAC field hockey title, beats defending champion Darien for Class L crown
item.description: Fairfield Ludlowe celebrates their 2-1 victory over Darien in the CIAC Class L Field Hockey Championship in Wethersfield on November 10, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) WETHERSFIELD - Three years, two semifinal heartbreaks and a job finally finished. The Ludlowe field hockey team won its first CIAC championship Saturday in Wethersfield, beating No. 1 seed and defending champion Darien 2-1 to cap a mission that started when the current players were playing at the youth level. Darien had beaten Ludlowe twice previously this season, once in the regular season and again two weeks ago in the FCIAC championship game. "Looking back at that last game, I don't think we put up enough of a fight and made it easy for them to put in goals early against us," Ludlowe junior Lily McClay said. "This is a dream come true and means everything. I thought about this game every day and said a prayer every night and it finally happened." Ludlowe took an early lead with 3:24 left in the first quarter when Lily's sister, freshman Emerson McClay, kept the ball alive on the end line and was able to sneak it past the goalie for the crucial first goal. "When I insert (on corners), I try to go for rebounds and it was there and, to be honest, I didn't know if I was in the circle or not, and I was so happy when it went in," Emerson McClay said. "I wasn't sure if it was going to count, but it got us going." Emerson McClay would add a second goal with 5:45 left in the second quarter, putting Ludlowe up 2-0 at halftime. Darien would not go away and cut the deficit to one on a Skylar Stephens goal with 6:30 left. From there, the clock could not move fast enough for Ludlowe. "That was forever, the longest five minutes of my life, but we handled it well," Ludlowe coach Laura McClay, Lily and Emerson's mother, said. "We are thrilled. I could not be happier for this group and these seniors." Darien was playing in its fifth straight Class L final and 19th overall, but did not have enough to snag back-to-back titles. "From the get-go, the ball wasn't bouncing our way," Darien coach Mo Minicus said. "They went up 2-0 with our mistakes, but we hung in there and fought and out-cornered them and out-shot them, but their goalie played great. We didn't get the tips, we didn't get the rebounds, but I am proud of the girls and proud of their fight." Ludlowe goalie Erin McNamara made eight saves, including one diving effort in the first half to preserve the lead. MSU's win over Detroit was predictably clunky, but way closer than it should have been EAST LANSING — If you were wondering what Jordan Scott and Coen Carr mean to this Michigan State basketball team, here’s the answer: MSU 91, Detroit Mercy 70. The Titans were hitting rainbows from 25 feet, sometimes over defenders. But the Spartans ’ first-half and early second-half defense helped them get hot. MSU, even shorthanded, was eventually a bit too much and avoided what would have been an upset of 2014 Texas-Southern proportions. If this game had gone that way, Tom Izzo might have taken another two decades off of this in-state rivalry, as he did from 2001 until 2020. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Drew Allar provided an encouraging update on his development before Week 11. Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers are aiming to win their first playoff game in a decade with Aaron Rodgers behind center this January. But the future Hall of Fame signal-caller isn’t the team’s future. That’s obvious. Rodgers will turn 43 years old in December. Who is the future at quarterback for the Steelers remains very uncertain. But 2026 third-round pick Drew Allar is doing what he can to ensure he’s ready when he gets his shot at being the solution. Allar has spent the 2026 campaign as the team’s backup to the emergency quarterback. In other words, he’s No. 4 on the depth chart, which makes him a non-factor on this year’s team. But Allar is still in a critical year of his development. According to the rookie, it’s going well. While speaking to reporters this past week, Allar shared a positive update on improvement at practice, particularly in his footwork. “I’m not thinking about it anymore,” Allar said, via Steelers insider Mark Kaboly . “Rookie minicamp, OTAs, and even the first part of camp, I’m out there thinking about everything, and I might be purposely slowing it down to get the right feel of what Coach Arth, Coach McCarthy, and Aaron are emphasizing. “To me, throughout each drill, I feel like I’m at the point now where I can go out and play game-like speed and really push myself to, you know, not just go out and play fast and still watch all the film from our QB (individual drills) to make sure I’m staying on top of the little things that I worked a lot on. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
